wy_upper_blair_boulder_problems.blurb: A loose scatter of small boulders in the Upper Blair part of Vedauwoo, outside Laramie, rather than one tidy bouldering cluster. Most of the ten climbs here are short boulder problems, mainly in the easy to moderate range with a couple of harder ones, plus a pair of trad lines and a single sport route. The mood is quiet and low-key: it suits a wanderer who likes some solitude, and most problems are easy to reach, so it works for a family or a dog. One of the taller boulders carries several problems, and a few lines finish with a hard or tall topout, so bring more than one pad.

_expect.name: Twin Towers Wall (aka Low Voltage Wall)

wy_twin_towers_wall_aka_low_voltage_wall.blurb: A small riverside wall in Fremont Canyon, the granite canyon cut by the North Platte in central Wyoming. Ten routes, nearly all of them bolted, with a single trad line. The grades spread from easy up through the 5.12 range, with the heaviest concentration around 5.9 and 5.10, so there is something for newer leaders as well as people looking for a harder pitch. The wall faces south and catches plenty of sun. Routes are short, and the foot of the wall has a flat spot for sitting and belaying right beside the water. Getting down involves a scramble and a bit of brush.

wy_upper_psychoactive_wall.blurb: A sport wall in the Leigh Creek zone of Ten Sleep Canyon, found by crossing the creek and continuing up the slope to the right-hand side of the main cliff band. All ten routes are bolted and the grades start around 5.10 and climb steeply: a handful of 5.11s, a few 5.12s and a couple of 5.13s, so this is more a wall for people working at their limit than for warm-ups. The limestone is peanut-buttery low down and improves higher up. The wall stays in shade nearly all day through most of the year, which helps on hot afternoons.
